ceiling_statement: Maximum achievable legal-reasoning correctness under H1-H8 is: provable soundness AND completeness of every emitted legal conclusion with respect to the unique grounded (well-founded) extension of an explicitly committed, finite, defeasible rulebase, where (a) every conclusion carries a machine-checkable derivation certificate re-verifiable offline (H5/H8), (b) defeater sensitivity is total over the committed rulebase (every admitted defeater that attacks a derivation is guaranteed to defeat or be defeated in the labelling, including cyclic attack structures, which terminate with label :out/:undefined), and (c) every question whose answer depends on unformalized or interpretively contested source text returns typed UNKNOWN (H2). No feasible system can additionally guarantee correctness of the natural-language-to-rule formalization step itself, nor resolve genuinely contested interpretation.
derivation: Three independent limits pin this ceiling. (1) Computability: full first-order defeasible logic is undecidable, and credulous acceptance under preferred/stable argumentation semantics is NP-hard and non-unique, violating H5 determinism; the grounded/well-founded semantics is the unique maximal semantics that is simultaneously deterministic (single minimal complete extension), polynomial-time computable (alternating-fixpoint on a finite lattice, hence provably terminating), and certificate-carrying (each label has a finite well-founded derivation tree). Any 'stronger' semantics either loses uniqueness (breaks H5 replay) or decidability (breaks H3 fail-closed termination). (2) Information theory: the bytes of a statute underdetermine its legal meaning (open texture; contested interpretation is not a computable function of the committed text), so correctness 'about the law itself' is not machine-decidable by ANY system; the supremum is correctness relative to a committed formal rulebase plus honest UNKNOWN at the formalization boundary. (3) H1 closes the only escape hatch: a statistical model cannot be trusted to certify the NL-to-formal mapping, so that mapping enters only as attested, admitted input whose certificate records who/what asserted it — never as trusted inference. Therefore sound+complete grounded-extension computation with derivation certificates plus typed UNKNOWN at the interpretation boundary is the ceiling; exceeding it requires deciding an undecidable or non-encoded question.
relativity_note: Relative to the grounded (well-founded) semantics of finite defeasible rule systems — Dung's grounded extension, equivalently the well-founded model of the corresponding logic program (Van Gelder-Ross-Schlipf). Correctness claims are meaningful only against this committed formal semantics of the admitted rulebase, never against 'the law' as natural-language text.

Prove: (T1) Φ has a unique least fixpoint wf(G) and the implemented iteration computes it in ≤ |N| rounds (termination + uniqueness, hence deterministic replay); (T2) soundness — every node labelled `in` by the implementation possesses a finite well-founded derivation tree all of whose defeaters are labelled `out`; (T3) completeness — every node `in` the well-founded model is labelled `in`; (T4) defeater sensitivity — adding any admitted defeater d attacking node n either flips n to out/undefined or yields a certificate that d is itself out; (T5) UNKNOWN monotonicity — `undefined` never satisfies the acceptance predicate (no upgrade to pass). ceiling_statement: Maximum achievable plan-decomposition assurance under H1-H8 is: for a plan committed as a finite, explicitly typed dataflow DAG with a declared goal-artifact set, ALL defects in the decidable defect class — cyclic dependency, produces/consumes artifact-type mismatch on any edge, goal artifact unreachable from admitted inputs, orphan stage feeding no goal, ambiguous execution order — are made structurally inadmissible at plan-definition time (fail-closed macroexpansion, H3), the admitted plan has a unique deterministic total schedule (H5), and the plan carries a certificate that any third party re-derives from the committed plan bytes alone (H8). No feasible system can additionally verify completeness of the plan relative to informal human intent, nor decide plan existence over unbounded action spaces.
derivation: (1) Verification theory: 'is this decomposition complete?' relative to intent is not computable — the intent is not encoded in the machine; the only machine-checkable question is completeness relative to a committed formal goal specification. This is model-independent underdetermination, identical in kind to AX-01's text/meaning gap. (2) Complexity: general plan synthesis (STRIPS-style) is PSPACE-complete and undecidable over infinite domains — but H5+H6 force the plan to exist as a committed finite artifact BEFORE execution (deterministic replay requires a frozen plan; all-or-nothing transitions require knowing the transition set). Against a committed finite DAG with finitely many typed edges, every property in the defect class above is decidable in O(V+E) and its certificate is checkable in linear time; therefore FULL exclusion of the decidable class, not statistical reduction of it, is feasible — and per the CLAUDE.md supreme law, elimination of the error class is the ceiling, guarding against instances is below it. (3) Determinism: among valid schedules, uniqueness is achievable at zero cost (topological sort with total lexicographic tie-break), and any nondeterministic schedule strictly violates H5, so the ceiling includes schedule uniqueness. Exceeding this ceiling would require either deciding intent (not encoded, information-theoretically impossible) or verifying unbounded plan spaces (undecidable).
relativity_note: Relative to the committed typed-DAG plan semantics: a finite set of stages with declared :produces/:consumes artifact types and a declared goal-artifact set (the DEFPIPELINE formalism of systems/orchestrator-spec/pipeline-dsl.lisp). 'Plan completeness' is completeness w.r.t. that committed goal set — never w.r.t. unformalized intent.

ceiling_statement: Maximum achievable contradiction/uncertainty/coverage/blind-spot handling under H1-H8 is trichotomous certified totality: every query against the committed corpus and rulebase returns exactly one of {PASS with recomputable certificate, FAIL/CONTRADICTION with recomputable counter-certificate, typed UNKNOWN carrying a machine-readable reason drawn from a CLOSED, committed enumeration of unknowability causes} — where (a) contradiction detection is provably complete WITHIN a declared decidable class over the committed inputs, (b) the boundary of that class is itself a committed, certificate-carrying, machine-enforced artifact (not prose), (c) coverage is a positively-proven census (absence of a check is itself a detectable, blocking state — no silent gap), and (d) UNKNOWN is a terminal object: no operation maps it to pass/equality (H2) and any flagged anomaly is a blocking, non-servable state (H3). No feasible system can additionally certify the absence of unknown-unknowns outside its committed input set, or decide consistency of theories beyond its declared decidable class.
derivation: (1) Computability: consistency of an unrestricted first-order theory is undecidable (and by Gödel II, an expressive consistent system cannot prove its own consistency), so 'detects all contradictions' is impossible simpliciter for ANY system; the supremum is completeness within a declared decidable class plus a checkable declaration of that class's boundary. (2) Information theory: blind spots over inputs never received are undetectable in principle — no computation over received bytes can bound properties of unreceived bytes; hence the ceiling for blind-spot handling is not 'no blind spots' but 'no SILENT blind spots over the committed universe': a positively-proven coverage census in which every element of the committed corpus is either checked (with certificate) or explicitly enumerated as unchecked (blocking or typed-UNKNOWN), so that within the commitment, unaccounted state is structurally impossible. This is the exact dual of a fail-open gate: absence of proof must be distinguishable from proof of absence, and only the committed universe admits that distinction. (3) Consistency/verification theory: a false-green (claiming coverage or consistency not actually recomputed) is excluded only by H8 recompute-and-compare — a declared 'all clear' can never exceed what an independent recomputation over committed inputs establishes. Therefore trichotomous certified totality with a closed UNKNOWN-reason enumeration and a positively-proven census is the ceiling; every stronger claim collides with undecidability (b), unreceived-input opacity (2), or producer-trust (3). This argument is model-independent — it holds for any system whatsoever satisfying H1-H8.

Prove: (T1) totality — V is a total function (no query lacks a verdict); (T2) certificate soundness — pass/fail certificates re-verify under the independent checker (recompute-and-compare, zero producer trust); (T3) in-class completeness — for every pair (r1, r2) in the committed rulebase, conflict r1 r2 = true implies V returns fail with a counter-certificate naming (r1, r2) (exhaustive detection within the decidable class); (T4) census positivity — for every (c, u) ∈ C × U, the coverage matrix contains exactly one of {checked-with-cert, enumerated-unchecked}, and a missing entry is unrepresentable in the manifest type (no silent gap, by construction); (T5) UNKNOWN terminality — no function in the trusted API maps `unknown r` to `pass` (stated as: the pass-introduction rules of the Verdict algebra never take an unknown argument — a typing theorem). ceiling_statement: For any system satisfying H1-H8, the maximum attainable grounding of a served legal text t is: (i) ORIGIN AUTHENTICITY no stronger than what can be TRANSPORTED or CORROBORATED — either verification of the official publisher's cryptographic signature over the captured bytes (transport), or agreement of a k-of-n quorum of independent, contemporaneous capture witnesses over the byte digest (corroboration), with anything below that admissible only as typed UNKNOWN/provisional; plus (ii) DERIVATION BINDING — a deterministic, third-party re-executable extraction function E with byte-equality E(captured-bytes) = t, committed as a dual digest (source-digest, extraction-digest); plus (iii) CORPUS-SIZE INDEPENDENCE — the truth of Grounded(t) mentions only the committed capture record of t's own source (selection by exact committed identifier, never by search/glob/statistics), so it is invariant under corpus extension, with verification cost O(log n) via Merkle inclusion. No feasible system exceeds this triple.
derivation: Part (i) is information-theoretic: authenticity of bytes fetched from a network endpoint cannot be created after the fact by any local computation — a digest commits to WHAT was received, never to WHO published it. The only two mechanisms that add origin assurance are (a) verifying a signature whose key predates the capture and roots in the publisher (authenticity is transported through the signature, bounded by the publisher's PKI), and (b) independent corroboration: if k witnesses on disjoint trust/network paths commit the same digest at capture time, forging the origin requires compromising all k or the publisher endpoint itself — a Byzantine-agreement-style bound that no single-observer scheme can match and no scheme can exceed without (a). H1 forbids substituting a statistical model's judgment of authenticity; H8 forbids trusting the producer's declared root, so recompute-over-committed-bytes is forced. Part (ii) is a verification-theory limit: 'served text derives from primary bytes' is checkable by a zero-trust third party ONLY if the derivation is a pure deterministic function (H5) whose re-execution can be compared byte-for-byte — any nondeterministic or judgment-bearing extraction step is unverifiable in principle offline, so the ceiling is exactly deterministic-replay equality. Part (iii): any grounding predicate that consults corpus-global state (search ranking, glob resolution, frequency) makes admissibility of one text depend on unrelated texts, which both breaks replay under corpus growth (H5/H7) and adds zero authenticity (corpus statistics carry no information about the gazette's bytes); commitment-based membership needs Θ(log n) with Merkle trees, and O(log n) suffices for feasibility, so per-item cost independent of semantic corpus content is attainable and nothing structurally better exists without trusted state.

lean_obligation: Model captures, witnesses, and extraction abstractly: given `hash : Bytes → Digest` (collision-resistant, axiom), `E : Bytes → ServedText` a total computable function, `sigOK : PublisherKey → Bytes → Sig → Prop`, and a finite witness set W each committing a digest at capture time. Define `Grounded (t : ServedText) (c : Capture) : Prop := (∃ s, sigOK pk c.bytes s ∨ ∃ (Q : Finset Witness), Q.card ≥ k ∧ ∀ w ∈ Q, w.commit = hash c.bytes) ∧ E c.bytes = t`. Prove: (T-ceiling) any grounding predicate P satisfying H5 (decidable by pure offline recomputation over committed data) and H8 (no producer-declared root trusted) implies P t → Grounded t, i.e. Grounded is the supremum; (T-attain) the system's admission predicate equals Grounded; (T-size-indep) monotonicity/invariance: for corpora C ⊆ C', Grounded t c holds in C ↔ in C' (the predicate never mentions |C|), and Merkle inclusion verification is O(log |C|).

ceiling_statement: Relative to a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order and a fixed authority-chain semantics, the maximum attainable by any H1-H8 system is: SOUND AND COMPLETE PROOF-CARRYING RESOLUTION OVER L(G) — every string in L(G) occurring in served text is parsed by a total, coverage-gated recognizer and resolved to exactly one committed authority record carrying a verified receipt (signature chain valid to a pinned owner key, delegation valid at the receipt's genTime, revocation checked, bitemporal validity interval covering the citation's reference time), and every citation-like string outside L(G) is emitted as typed UNKNOWN-CITATION that never upgrades to a pass (H2). Beyond this ceiling lie two things NO feasible system can deliver: recognition of arbitrary natural-language reference intent outside G, and verification that the cited authority semantically supports the citing proposition — both are excluded, and any claim to deliver them without human adjudication is structurally dishonest under H1.
derivation: Computability limit: the set of natural-language strings that 'function as a citation' has no decidable characterization — surface forms are open-ended and reference intent is a semantic property of text, so by a Rice-style argument no algorithm decides it for arbitrary input; any total mechanical recognizer necessarily fixes a formal language, hence the ceiling can only be stated relative to a declared decidable G. H1 closes the only escape route: a statistical model approximating NL intent is exactly what the invariant bans from the trusted path, so its output can at most be an untrusted CANDIDATE that must re-enter through the G-verifier — it cannot raise the trusted ceiling above L(G). Within L(G), verification theory gives the exact maximum: a citation is validated when it is bound to an authority record whose authenticity chain is checkable offline with zero producer trust (H8) — signature verification against a pinned root, delegation window containment, revocation absence, and bitemporal validity are each decidable predicates over committed data, and their conjunction is the strongest offline-checkable statement about a citation's TARGET; nothing stronger exists because authority-ness beyond the committed chain (e.g. 'this court's PDF is genuine') reduces to the AX-04 origin ceiling. The semantic-support question (does the authority actually stand for the proposition?) requires an oracle for legal meaning; no formal semantics of open-textured law that is both sound and complete exists today, so under H2 the only honest output for it is UNKNOWN. Consistency: the JWS layer proves internal consistency, not authenticity — authenticity enters only through the pinned-owner chain, which is why the ceiling names the chain, not the timestamp.
relativity_note: Relative to: (1) a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order (for B0: Greek FEK/ELI references — the executable grammar to be seated where source/citation-authority.lisp and source/legal-references.lisp now hold regexes); (2) the TUF-style delegation semantics of authority-v2/roles/ROLES-MODEL.sexp with Ed25519 owner-pinning as implemented in source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp; (3) the bitemporal validity semantics of source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp (valid-time × transaction-time, genTime floor). Change any of the three and the ceiling statement changes with it.

lean_obligation: Fix G as an inductive grammar with decidable membership `decG : ∀ s : String, Decidable (s ∈ L G)`, receipts `R` with `chainValid : R → Prop` (signature to pinned root, delegation window, non-revoked — each a decidable predicate over committed bytes) and `validAt : R → Time → Prop` (bitemporal containment). Let `resolve : {s // s ∈ L G} → Option R` be the system's pure resolver and `out : String → Result` its total output function. Prove: (SOUND) `∀ s h r, out s = .cited r → s ∈ L G ∧ resolve ⟨s,h⟩ = some r ∧ chainValid r ∧ validAt r (refTime s)`; (COMPLETE-rel-G) `∀ s, s ∈ L G → out s ≠ .dropped` (every grammar hit is either a verified receipt or a typed failure, never silent); (HONEST) `∀ s, s ∉ L G → out s = .unknown`, and `.unknown` is not equal to and never coerces to `.cited _` (H2 as a type-level impossibility); (CEILING) any output function satisfying H1/H5/H8 that claims `.cited r` on some s ∉ L G contradicts decidability-of-trusted-path — i.e. the trusted validated set is at most `{s | s ∈ L G ∧ chainValid (resolve s)}`.

ceiling_statement: The maximum evidence-provenance and transformation-lineage assurance attainable by any H1-H8 system is PER-STEP RECOMPUTE-AND-COMPARE OVER A COMMITTED PURE-TRANSFORMATION DAG, TOTAL OVER THE RELEASE CLOSURE: every trusted artifact in a release has a lineage chain of steps (input-hash, deterministic-transformation-id, output-hash) whose edges are committed under a domain-separated Merkle root bound inside the signed release identity, such that a zero-trust offline verifier re-executes each declared transformation and compares output bytes, with any artifact lacking a complete chain — or any step failing byte-equality — blocking the release (fail-closed totality). Assurance is bounded exactly by (a) the collision resistance of the commitment hash, (b) the purity/determinism of each declared step, and (c) the AX-04 origin ceiling at the chain's roots; nothing feasible exceeds this.
derivation: Three independent limits pin this ceiling, each model-independent. (1) Information-theoretic: un-committed history is unrecoverable — a verifier can establish facts only about data that was committed at production time; no amount of later computation reconstructs which transformation actually ran if only aggregate endpoints were recorded. Hence per-step commitment is not a design choice but the information-theoretic maximum granularity of verifiable lineage; an aggregate base-hash/result-hash + step-count (B0's consolidation ledger today) provably admits distinct histories with identical aggregates, so it sits strictly below the ceiling. (2) Verification theory: with zero producer trust (H8) the verifier may not accept any declared intermediate — the only operation that converts a lineage CLAIM into lineage KNOWLEDGE is re-executing the step and comparing bytes, which is possible precisely when the step is a pure deterministic function (H5: no wall-clock/RNG/IO in the decision); an impure or nondeterministic step is unverifiable offline in principle, so the ceiling covers exactly the pure-step DAG and honest systems must type anything else as UNKNOWN (H2). Recompute-and-compare is therefore both necessary and sufficient — the same argument that makes AX-13's 'offline verifiability cannot exceed recompute-and-compare' absolute. (3) Completeness is a closure property, not a per-artifact property: 'lineage-complete' means the lineage function is TOTAL over the transitive closure of the release — and totality over a finite committed set is decidable by census, so a fail-closed census gate (H3) attains the maximum; no system can exceed totality. Cost floor: verifying n artifacts with s total steps requires Ω(s) recomputation plus O(s log n) inclusion checks; this is feasible today and optimal up to the log factor without trusted state. The whole construction rests on one cryptographic assumption (SHA-256 collision resistance) plus the AX-04 ceiling at the roots — provenance can never exceed the authenticity of its terminal inputs.

ceiling_statement: For any feasible system under H1-H8, institutional/reflective memory can guarantee at most: (a) provenance-complete capture - every certified state transition (H6) is committed as an episode carrying content digests of all inputs that decided it, so each remembered decision is offline-replayable (H5); (b) tamper-evidence by full recomputation - an offline verifier holding only the log bytes recomputes the whole hash chain from canonical episode bodies and detects any mutation, deletion, insertion, or reorder of any committed episode, up to hash collision-resistance (H8: recompute-and-compare, never trust the declared head); (c) rollback/fork detection exactly relative to the verifier's freshest previously-held committed checkpoint (prefix-consistency against any held prior head) - the fork-consistency bound; (d) recall as a pure deterministic function of the committed prefix, with typed UNKNOWN for anything never committed (H2). No feasible system can exceed (c) without a live external witness quorum, can remember what was not committed at event time, or can attest its own live in-RAM state (only its committed prefix).
derivation: Three independent limits. (1) Information-theoretic no-retrodiction: memory at time t is a function of bytes committed by t; an uncommitted observation is absent from every later verification, so provenance-complete capture at commit time is the maximum, and H2 forces UNKNOWN rather than reconstruction for gaps. (2) Fork-consistency bound (Mazieres-Shasha / SUNDR): with an untrusted producer and a verifier whose only input is the log bytes (H8 zero producer trust), two distinct well-formed histories are indistinguishable - internal consistency is verifiable but 'this is THE history' is not; the only escapes are a verifier-held prior checkpoint (yielding prefix-consistency relative to that floor) or an external witness quorum, which is a deployment resource B0 honestly declares NIL (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp: external_quorum_status = disabled). Hence checkpoint-relative rollback detection is the hard ceiling for a single-organization deployment. (3) Self-verification limit: a process cannot produce a producer-trust-free proof of its own current runtime state (any such proof is produced by the state being attested); under H8 only the committed, externally recomputable prefix is verifiable, so 'reflective memory' maxes out at reflection over the committed chain, not over live RAM. Within these bounds, single-writer serialization (H4) plus hash chaining with the chain discipline sealed inside the hashed body attains every guarantee the limits permit - so the ceiling is attained, not merely approached.

ceiling_statement: For any feasible system under H1-H8, temporal and legal-state consistency can guarantee at most: (a) gapless monotone history - every admitted transition satisfies seq' = seq + 1 exactly, serialized through a single-writer admission point, so system history is a certificate-carrying total order with no gaps, repeats, or rollback (H4/H6); (b) append-only verifiability - any verifier holding any prior committed root verifies, by recomputing an RFC-6962 consistency proof, that the current log extends it; a verifier with no prior root can verify internal consistency only (wholesale replacement is undetectable to a fresh verifier - the fork-consistency bound, liftable only by an external witness quorum, a resource honestly absent today); (c) bitemporal legal-state soundness - the assertion 'legal state at valid-time t as known at transaction-time tau' is at most a pure, offline-replayable function (H5/H8) of the source snapshots and typed amendment events committed by tau under a declared formal amendment semantics, returning typed UNKNOWN (H2) for any (t, tau) not covered by committed evidence. No feasible system can assert legal state beyond its committed evidence, anticipate unpublished amendments, or exceed checkpoint-relative anti-rollback without real external witnesses.
derivation: (1) Evidence bound (information-theoretic): at transaction-time tau the system possesses exactly the bytes it has committed; an amendment the publisher has issued but the system has not captured is informationally absent, so the map (t, tau) -> state cannot exceed a function of the committed corpus at tau - and H1/H2 forbid statistical interpolation of the gap, forcing typed UNKNOWN. (2) Purity bound (verification theory): H5 + H8 require the (t, tau) view to be recomputable by a third party from committed inputs alone; any 'fresher' answer would depend on producer-declared, non-replayable state, violating H8 - so the deterministic bitemporal view over committed snapshots IS the ceiling, not an approximation of it. (3) Fork-consistency bound (Mazieres-Shasha): the transparency log alone proves internal append-only consistency; distinguishing the true history from a consistent fabricated one requires either a verifier-held prior root (prefix theorem via RFC-6962 consistency proofs) or a cosigning witness quorum - the latter is RESOURCE-dependent and B0 declares it disabled with no split-view-resistance claim (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp line 15), so consumer-floor-relative anti-rollback is the attainable maximum today. (4) Serialization bound (consistency/CAP-style): exactly-once gapless sequence increment requires a serialization point; a single-writer kernel (H4) attains it directly, and no coordination-free distributed scheme can guarantee it without consensus resources not declared here. In-force/implicit-repeal determinations are additionally interpretation-laden, which is why the legal-state half of the ceiling is only definable relative to a named formal amendment semantics.

Sub-bounds (a) and (b) - gapless monotone sequence and recompute-verified append-only consistency - are ABSOLUTE (model-independent); only the legal-state half (c) is semantics-relative, since 'in force at t' (vacatio legis, implicit repeal) has no model-free ground truth.

ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible coordination under H1-H8 is CONFLUENT DETERMINISTIC PARALLELISM WITH ATOMIC TIER COMMIT: stages may execute concurrently exactly when they form an antichain of the declared dependency DAG with pairwise-disjoint write footprints; the committed result is bitwise equal to the unique canonical serial execution (fixed topological order with deterministic tie-break); wall-clock speedup is bounded below by max(T_work/p, T_span) over the DAG's critical path (Brent's work-span law) for p declared workers; and all inter-agent arbitration is reduced to deterministic, data-defined admission at one kernel-enforced writer seat — never to timing, races, or votes. Any stage failure aborts its entire tier with the pre-tier state restored exactly.
derivation: Three independent limits compose. (1) Consistency/replay limit: H5 (deterministic replay, pure derivations) plus H8 (third-party recompute-and-compare) require the committed output to be a function of frozen inputs alone. A parallel execution whose result can depend on interleaving of non-commuting effects is not a function of its inputs, so it is unreplayable — hence the Church-Rosser condition (concurrent steps must commute, i.e., disjoint write footprints within an antichain, with a deterministic merge order) is not an engineering choice but the outer boundary: no feasible system can admit more concurrency than the commuting fraction of its effect algebra without forfeiting H5/H8. (2) Scheduling limit: given that boundary, the work-span law T_p >= max(T_1/p, T_inf) is information-flow arithmetic on the DAG — dependent stages carry data dependencies no scheduler can bypass except by speculation, and under H6 (all-or-nothing certified transitions) speculative state may never become visible in the trusted store, so speculation can only discard work, never raise the span bound. (3) Arbitration limit: FLP shows deterministic asynchronous consensus among peers is impossible with even one fault; H4 (single seat, single-writer canonical truth) dissolves the consensus problem structurally — every agent output is an untrusted candidate (H1) and the only lawful arbitration is a deterministic decidable admission predicate evaluated at the one writer seat, enforced below the code by kernel DAC (EACCES), which is the strongest arbitration available on a single-authority operating model. H3 forces the failure semantics: a failed stage cannot be 'marked executed'; the only fail-closed option is tier abort with exact pre-tier state, which requires the tier commit to be atomic (ties to AX-11).

ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible transaction semantics for workflow/tool orchestration under H1-H8 is: (i) for all effects on media the system controls — strict-serializable, single-commit-point atomicity: a multi-object transition (the six-item set of STORAGE-API.sexp) becomes visible through exactly one atomic switch, with durability exactly at the platform's fsync barrier and read-back-verified persistence, such that after a crash at ANY instant the recovered state is exactly sigma_pre or exactly sigma_post — never a hybrid; (ii) for effects on media the system does NOT control (network calls to external tools/publishers) — exactly-once is unattainable; the ceiling is journaled intent/outcome with idempotency keys and compensations, with the irrevocable external act structurally excluded from the atomic section. No feasible system exceeds (i) or circumvents (ii).
derivation: (i) is a storage-physics and protocol-theory bound. Stable storage exposes only bounded atomic units (a sector / an atomic rename of a directory entry) and reorders un-fenced writes; therefore any multi-object atomicity must be MANUFACTURED by funneling all objects' validity through one atomic commit record reached after fsync barriers — write-ahead logging and shadow-paging are the only two families, and both bottom out in a single atomic pointer/record switch. You cannot be 'more atomic' than one atomic switch, and you cannot be durable earlier than the fsync that puts the commit record on stable media: before that instant the information physically is not on the medium, so no protocol can promise it survives power loss. Read-back verification is the ceiling of durability EVIDENCE (H8: never trust a declared write). (ii) is the atomic-commitment impossibility: committing atomically across parties with independent failure modes requires a coordinator round (2PC), which blocks on coordinator failure and in the two-generals limit cannot be made both non-blocking and safe; since external publishers/tools grant the system no transactional interface at all, the honest ceiling is intent-journal before the call, outcome-journal after, idempotency keys for at-least-once retry, and compensation — with H3 demanding that an unknowable external outcome parks the workflow in a typed UNKNOWN state (H2) rather than guessing. H6 then fixes the composition: a workflow of many tool steps is accountable only if every trusted-state mutation routes through the single atomic commit of (i), making 'partial workflow effects in the canonical store' structurally impossible rather than guarded — exactly the error-class-elimination the supreme law demands.

(used at source/adoption-decision.lisp:99); (6) the single-writer premise of the protocol is the already-proven OS-DAC closure (authority-v2/proofs/verify-capability-closure.sh); (7) external tool calls (e.g. source/government-source.lisp fetches) move to an intent/outcome journal with idempotency keys OUTSIDE the atomic section, their products entering the store only as candidates through the commit. ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible institutional decision authority under H1-H8 is: every trusted state transition (adoption, release, retraction, override) is admitted by one total, pure, decidable kernel predicate K(state, transition, certificate) evaluated at the single writer seat, where acceptance yields a certificate-carrying, sequence-monotonic transition and EVERY other outcome — including an error inside the gate's own predicates — is a recorded, signed refusal with zero state change (fail-closed totality); authorization validity is offline-decidable by any third party recomputing the capability/delegation chain from a committed genesis trust anchor, which no system can eliminate (signatures transfer trust, they cannot create it); machine authority extends exactly to authorization and process compliance, never to the substantive rightness of the institutional decision itself, which remains with the accountable human creator; and absent a real external witness quorum, equivocation resistance is capped at fork consistency — a lying single writer can maintain divergent views, but any two views that ever meet yield producer-attributable cryptographic evidence (two signed checkpoints for the same sequence).
derivation: Four limits. (1) Verification theory: an offline verifier (H8, zero producer trust) can check only decidable predicates over committed bytes; therefore accountable authority is maximized precisely when admission IS a decidable proof-checking problem — certificate-carrying transitions — and cannot exceed it: any 'authority' not reified as a checkable certificate over committed inputs is unverifiable assertion, which H8 rates as zero. (2) Trust-anchor necessity: every signature chain terminates in a key whose bindingness is an axiom (genesis); information-theoretically a verifier with no prior trusted bit can authenticate nothing, so the ceiling is a minimal, committed, explicit genesis anchor — not its elimination. (3) Fail-closed totality (H2+H3): a gate predicate that errors has produced UNKNOWN, and H2 forbids UNKNOWN upgrading to pass; hence the ceiling gate maps every non-proof path to refusal, and — because H6 demands accountability of refusals too — the refusal itself must be a derivation (which article, which conjunct, over which committed facts), durably recorded. Nothing stronger exists: 'never wrongly refuse' would require deciding properties of arbitrary future predicates (Rice's theorem), so the ceiling keeps refusal cheap, recorded, and creator-overridable ONLY via an explicit, reason-carrying, logged override (never silent). (4) Equivocation bound (SUNDR result): with a single writer and no independent witnesses, fork consistency is the provable maximum — clients cannot detect a fork they never compare across; full split-view resistance requires an external cosigning quorum, which is not within unilateral reach today (B0 honestly declares witnesses NIL), so the honest ceiling claim is fork-consistency-with-evidence, not split-view immunity. The 'process not substance' clause follows from H1: judging legal-substantive correctness would put a model in the trusted path; the ceiling system makes the boundary of its own authority a committed, checkable artifact.

ceiling_statement: Maximum auditability is: every trusted output ships with a certificate that binds it, via collision-resistant hash commitments, to the COMPLETE closure of its derivation (source bytes, code identity, pinned toolchain identity, configuration, ordering schedule), such that an independent third party holding only the certificate and the committed closure can, fully offline and with zero producer trust, byte-identically RECOMPUTE the output and compare it to the commitment. Auditability terminates at the commitment boundary: nothing outside the committed closure (e.g., what the publisher's web server 'really' served at capture time) is auditable in principle — the strongest attainable is a signed/witnessed capture receipt committing the bytes at ingestion.
derivation: Verification theory admits exactly two zero-trust offline verification modes: (a) recompute-and-compare the derivation, or (b) check a succinct cryptographic proof of it. Mode (b) cannot exceed (a) in assurance — it adds trust in the proof system's soundness and in a correct arithmetization of the full semantics, and arithmetizing an SBCL pipeline is infeasible today — so recompute-and-compare over committed inputs is the ceiling, which is precisely H8's form. The boundary claim is information-theoretic: two histories producing identical committed byte-closures are indistinguishable to any auditor, so no audit can attest to anything not captured in the commitment; past states of external sources are not replayable, hence capture receipts are the maximum for origin bytes. Completeness of the closure is the only free variable, and 'complete' is capped by what was committed — an audit is exactly as strong as the closure is total. Ceiling holds for ANY system under H1–H8 modulo standard collision-resistance of the hash (SHA-256).

ceiling_statement: Maximum determinism is: every trusted derivation is a total mathematical function of its committed input closure — byte-identical output on every re-execution, on any machine, at any time — where the closure explicitly includes every reified nondeterminism source (logical clock value, any seed, the parallel merge schedule, canonical orderings, and the pinned toolchain identity). Equivalently: the ONLY nondeterminism anywhere in the system lives outside the trusted path (LLM candidates, network fetches) and crosses into it solely as committed bytes. Byte-identity is the terminal point: no stronger equivalence than bit equality exists.
derivation: A computation's output can depend only on its inputs; therefore determinism is maximal exactly when the input set is closed — every read of wall-clock, RNG, scheduler order, hash-table iteration, address-dependent hashing, or filesystem enumeration is either banished from the trusted path or converted into a committed input. Nothing can exceed 'output = f(committed closure)': any residual dependence on an uncommitted quantity is, by definition, nondeterminism. Byte-identity across machines requires the implementation semantics be part of the closure (pinned SBCL version, IEEE-754 float behavior) — that is a closure item, not a weakening, so the ceiling stays model-independent. Two things NO feasible system can do, and the ceiling honestly excludes: determinizing the untrusted producers themselves (H1 confines them instead), and determinism against hardware faults (bit flips) — the attainable form there is detection by AX-13 recompute-and-compare, not prevention. This is also H5 stated as a maximum.

ceiling_statement: On the declared operating model (single node, POSIX filesystem, commodity SSD with honored write barriers), the maximum achievable is: (a) DURABILITY — a state transition is durable exactly when its data, metadata, and directory entry have reached stable media behind an explicit write barrier (fsync of file AND containing directory); acknowledged-but-unsynced data is unrecoverable in principle; single-device durability is bounded by media survival — nothing short of replication (out of the declared model) exceeds it. (b) CRASH CONSISTENCY — atomicity of accountable transitions: after a crash at ANY point, recovery yields a state equal to applying some prefix of the committed transition sequence, with every barrier-acknowledged transition included and no torn/partial artifact ever observable (H6 as a maximum). (c) BOUNDED RECOVERY — recovery work is Θ(uncommitted tail since last checkpoint), which checkpointing caps by a constant; no scheme recovers in less than the time to read what recovery must read. (d) Fail-closed read-back: a transition counts committed only after recompute-and-compare of the persisted bytes (H3/H8).
derivation: Storage physics: volatile memory does not survive power loss, so durability of information not yet behind a stable-media barrier is information-theoretically impossible — the fsync wait is not an implementation choice but the definition of the durable point. Atomicity: the storage stack provides only small atomic primitives (single-sector write; POSIX rename within a filesystem); any larger atomic unit must be constructed by a commit protocol (WAL or shadow-paging via temp+rename), and every such protocol needs at least one ordering barrier separating data from the commit record — without it the device may reorder and expose torn state; hence 'intent → data fsync → atomic rename/commit record → directory fsync' is not one design among many but the minimal shape any correct protocol reduces to. Prefix semantics is the consistency ceiling: a crash can land between any two barriers, so the strongest invariant any single-node system can promise is 'some committed prefix, monotone, nothing torn' — promising more (e.g., zero lost acknowledged-unsynced writes) violates physics; promising less (fail-open partial states) violates H3/H6. Recovery lower bound is trivial counting: recovery must at least read the journal tail it replays.

ceiling_statement: Under the declared operating model (single node, fair scheduler, eventually-available storage, finite committed inputs, external calls that may fail forever), the maximum achievable liveness is CONDITIONAL BOUNDED TERMINATION: every admitted task reaches, within an explicit per-task budget B(task), exactly one of three terminal states — SUCCESS with certificate, typed FAIL, or typed UNKNOWN/REFUSED — with no livelock, no unbounded retry, and no silent hang; retries are idempotent so a re-attempt after partial failure has exactly-once observable effect on committed state; after a crash, work resumes from the last checkpoint with bounded re-execution. Unconditional liveness (progress no matter what the environment does) is UNACHIEVABLE by any system honoring H3 — blocking on persistent environment misbehavior is forced, and the ceiling converts every such block into a typed, bounded-time refusal rather than a hang.
derivation: Three impossibility facts pin the ceiling. (1) Fail-closed vs. progress trade-off: H3 requires blocking on error/violation/unknown; an adversarial environment (storage returning EIO forever, origin never serving valid bytes) can therefore stall any H3-compliant system indefinitely — so 'progress' can only ever be conditional on declared environment assumptions; the maximum is making the condition explicit and the failure mode a bounded-time typed refusal (H2) instead of a hang. This is the single-node analogue of FLP: safety-preserving systems buy liveness only from environment assumptions. (2) Exactly-once effects: at-least-once retry plus at-most-once effect is achievable only via idempotence/deduplication state — exactly-once delivery without a dedup record is classically impossible — so idempotency-keyed retries checked against a durable journal are the ceiling mechanism, not an option; without them retries violate H6 all-or-nothing. (3) Termination cannot be inferred: by Rice/halting, a system cannot decide termination of arbitrary loops, so the maximum feasible guarantee is termination BY CONSTRUCTION — every trusted loop carries a well-founded variant (strictly decreasing measure or finite budget), making non-termination structurally impossible rather than tested-for. Bounded recovery follows from AX-15's checkpoint bound.

ceiling_statement: For latency over a frozen workload distribution, the maximum assurance any H1–H8 system can provide is: (a) an EXACT, offline-verifiable deterministic cost certificate — for every workload item x, a cost value C(f,x) in abstract units (operations executed, bytes hashed, bytes consed, stage invocations) that any third party recomputes to bit-equality, so every quantile of the cost distribution over the frozen workload is a theorem, not a sample; plus (b) a fail-closed cost-budget gate that blocks any run whose certified cost exceeds a committed budget; plus (c) a wall-clock claim that is at most 'certified cost × attested machine rate r', where r is a signed measurement on declared hardware that is irreducibly attestation-trusted — no system can make wall-clock seconds themselves offline-verifiable with zero producer trust.
derivation: Two-part limit. (1) No-go on verified wall-clock: H5 requires trusted derivations to be pure functions of committed inputs, and H8 requires verification by recompute-and-compare. Wall-clock duration is not a function of committed inputs — it depends on scheduler interleaving, cache/thermal state, and hardware, so an independent verifier replaying the same committed inputs obtains a different number; recompute-and-compare over a non-recomputable quantity is undefined. Hence any wall-clock figure can only be a signed measurement (attested), never a zero-trust-verified fact; the offline-verifiable content of a latency claim is bounded above by what IS a pure function of inputs: the abstract cost of the deterministic execution path. (2) Exactness of the attainable part: because H5 makes the derivation deterministic, the multiset {C(f,x) : x ∈ frozen workload} is a computable function of the committed workload — its mean, p50, p99, and max are exactly computable and re-derivable by any verifier; statistical sampling error is eliminated entirely, which no measurement-based (non-frozen, non-pure) system can achieve. H3 then permits the strongest enforcement compatible with the no-go: a fail-closed budget gate on the certified cost (blocking, not advisory), while the seconds-conversion factor r remains a declared-resource attestation. Nothing feasible today exceeds this split: sublinear or hardware-independent verified timing would require either verified-hardware timing channels (not available) or trusting the producer's clock (violates H8).

ceiling_statement: Resource-normalized throughput of any H1–H8 system on p workers is bounded by T_p ≥ max(W/p, S, n·c_commit): W = total verification/generation work, S = span (critical path) of the input dependency DAG, and n·c_commit = the irreducibly SERIAL cost of appending n accountable transitions to the single-writer monotonic certificate sequence (H4/H6). Verification work W itself has an information-theoretic floor: a zero-producer-trust verifier (H8, recompute-and-compare) must read and hash every committed byte at least once, so throughput can never exceed the declared hardware's min(I/O bandwidth, hash bandwidth) per admitted byte; on unchanged inputs, content-addressed memoization reduces work to the delta plus one digest comparison per cached unit — its floor. The ceiling is attained by a deterministic parallel-map with ordered serial fold: embarrassingly parallel per-item verification saturating p workers, a single serialized commit seat with O(log n) Merkle proof material per append, and all bounds (worker count, batch sizes, item ranges) derived from committed corpus configuration rather than constants.
derivation: (1) Serial-commit floor: H4 (single-writer canonical truth) plus H6 (monotonic, all-or-nothing certificate sequence) force a total order on admissions — a single-copy linearizable log; by the standard consistency argument a totally ordered certificate chain cannot be committed by two writers concurrently without either forking the sequence (violating H6 monotonicity) or coordinating through what is again a single serialization point; hence commit throughput is bounded by the sequential rate of that point, and the best achievable is to make c_commit small (constant hashing per append, O(log n) proof size — the known optimum for verifiable append-only structures). (2) Work/span law (Brent): any schedule of the dependency DAG on p workers has makespan ≥ max(W/p, S) — a scheduling limit independent of implementation. (3) Verification floor: under H8 the verifier may not trust any declared root, so trusting k bytes requires reading k bytes — Ω(k) I/O and Ω(k) hashing; sublinear verification requires succinct proof systems (SNARKs) whose trusted setup and toolchain fall outside 'feasible today with standard cryptography', so recompute-and-compare's linear cost is the operative floor and hash/I-O bandwidth of the declared resources the operative ceiling. ceiling_statement: The maximum inspectable causal account any H1–H8 system can give for a trusted decision is the decision's own replayable derivation: a trace, recomputable to bit-equality by third parties from committed inputs (H5/H8), in which every trusted effect appears exactly once with its cause chain back to committed inputs, produced by a construction-level invariant making effect-execution and trace-emission the same event inside the same all-or-nothing transition (H6) — so an untraced trusted act is structurally impossible, not merely forbidden. Two hard limits bound this from above: (a) no explanation can carry more causal information than the derivation itself — every sound account is a function of the replay trace, so 'explanation = verified replay' is the supremum; (b) a causal account of WHY an untrusted candidate was proposed (LLM internals, H1) is unattainable and honestly out of scope — the complete explicable object is the admission/refusal derivation, which under H1 is the entire trusted causal story; completeness of the account is exactly the completeness of effect mediation (H4 capability closure), establishable structurally but not by static analysis of arbitrary code (Rice).
derivation: (1) Information-theoretic supremum: under H5 a trusted decision is a pure finite computation from committed inputs; the full derivation (the sequence of applied rules with their inputs) determines the decision and every true causal statement about it — any sound account is derivable from the trace, and any account not derivable from it asserts causation the computation does not contain (fabrication, barred by H2). Hence no system can explain a deterministic decision beyond its own replayed derivation; the ceiling is reached when the account IS the derivation and is verified by recompute (H8), never trusted as declared. (2) Structural completeness limit: 'the trace is complete' means no trusted effect escapes mediation. By Rice's theorem this cannot be decided by inspecting arbitrary program text; the only feasible route is making it structural — effects executable solely through capabilities (H4 closure), the capability mediator emitting the trace event in the same atomic transition as the effect (H6), so trace-omission implies effect-omission by construction. This converts an undecidable global property into a local invariant of one seat — the strongest form available without whole-program formal verification of the runtime. (3) H1 boundary: statistical-model internals admit no faithful causal account with today's tools, and H1 makes this irrelevant — the candidate is data, and the admission derivation over it is the complete causal account of everything the system asserts; a system claiming to 'explain' LLM internals would exceed what is verifiable and violate H2. (4) Determinism of the account: because the trace is a pure function of committed inputs, two independent verifiers derive identical accounts — explanation itself becomes replayable, a property no post-hoc sampled or interpretive explanation system can have.
